segments.text: Retrieves the current snapshot for the patch baseline the managed node uses. This API is primarily used by the [[p0]] Systems Manager document (SSM document).

If you run the command locally, such as with the Command Line Interface (CLI), the system attempts to use your local Amazon Web Services credentials and the operation fails. To avoid this, you can run the command in the Amazon Web Services Systems Manager console. Use Run Command, a tool in Amazon Web Services Systems Manager, with an SSM document that enables you to target a managed node with a script or command. For example, run the command using the [[p0]] document or the [[p1]] document.

A patch filter consists of a key and a set of values. The filter key is a patch property. For example, the available filter keys for [[p0]] are [[p1]] , [[p2]] , [[p3]] , [[p4]] , and [[p5]] .

The filter values define a matching criterion for the patch property indicated by the key. For example, if the filter key is [[p0]] and the filter values are [[p1]] , then the filter accepts all patches where product name is either “Office 2013” or “Office 2016”. The filter values can be exact values for the patch property given as a key, or a wildcard (*), which matches all values.

You can view lists of valid values for the patch properties by running the [[p0]] command. For information about which patch properties can be used with each major operating system, see DescribePatchProperties .
